primary_task: Write a README for the repository in the working directory from its actual source files, manifests and scripts.

requirements.name: Read/Glob/Grep
requirements.evidence: tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep, WebFetch, WebSearch; 'reading source files, tests, scripts, manifests'
requirements.basis: read: read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)

requirements.name: Bash (run help commands)
requirements.basis: bash: run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session

requirements.name: WebFetch/WebSearch
requirements.evidence: 'Search the web for framework context or missing standards only when the codebase is insufficient'
requirements.basis: web_search: search the public web and read result snippets | web_fetch: fetch a web page or unauthenticated API by URL; hosts outside the egress allow-list are refused

requirements.name: git commit/push
requirements.evidence: 'commit or push only if explicitly requested'
requirements.basis: bash: run shell commands on Linux x86_64: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads), build, test, run CLIs and scripts, git, gh, start and stop local servers inside the session

requirements.name: context manager
requirements.evidence: 'Query context manager for project purpose, target audience, and primary entry points'
requirements.basis: The manifest lists no context manager; the user can be asked via ask_user.

notes: Git commit/push is conditional on an explicit request, so not part of the primary task. If a push were required it reaches GitHub (open) but forbid_effects lists publishes.
